- **Isoxazole:** the ring runs O–N=C–C=C. Its C3 carries the NH, so it is an isoxazol-3-yl group, written `c2ccon2`.
- **Linker:** the NH connects to a CH2, which is attached by a hashed bond to C5 of the oxazolidinone.
- **Oxazolidin-2-one:** the ring runs O, C(=O), N, CH2, CH. The ring nitrogen is bonded to the aryl ring.
- **Aryl ring:** it has three fluorines and one CH. Going round from the carbon bearing the oxazolidinone N, the substituents are CH, F, N (the dihydropyridinone), F, F. The dihydropyridinone is N1–CH=CH–C(=O)–CH2–CH2, i.e. `N2C=CC(=O)CC2`.

For the stereocentre at C5, the substituents are the ring O (up), the ring CH2 (lower right), and the CH2NH (lower left, hashed, pointing away). The implicit H therefore points towards the viewer. From the H side, O → ring CH2 → CH2N runs clockwise. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order (O, H, CH2N, ring CH2) is an even permutation, so the centre is written `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C1O[C@@H](CNc2ccon2)CN1c1cc(F)c(N2C=CC(=O)CC2)c(F)c1F

name: Coprexa
text:
The image shows a Mo atom with two S atoms, each attached by a double bond (S=Mo=S), plus two separate [SH-] ions.

Reading the pieces:
- Each Mo=S bond is drawn as a double line, so the central unit is S=[Mo]=S.
- The two fragments below are drawn as "HS⁻", which gives [SH-] each.
- The fragments are disconnected, so they are separated by dots in the SMILES.

SMILES: [SH-].[SH-].S=[Mo]=S

name: Copper(II) acetylacetonate
text:
The drawing shows two identical acetylacetonate anions and one copper ion, with no bonds between the components.

Each anion is CH3–C(=O)–CH⁻–C(=O)–CH3. The central carbon carries a negative charge, and in SMILES it is written [CH-]. The copper is labelled Cu with a 2+ charge and a radical dot, so it is written [Cu+2] with the dot shown as a radical.

The radical dot in the label "Cu2+·" is a radical marker, so the copper is [Cu+2] with one unpaired electron, written [Cu++] in the drawing's convention. RDKit would write this as [Cu+2], and a radical-bearing form of it as [Cu+2].

Each anion in SMILES is CC(=O)[CH-]C(=O)C. The full molecule is two of these plus copper, joined by dots:

SMILES: CC(=O)[CH-]C(=O)C.CC(=O)[CH-]C(=O)C.[Cu+2]

name: Coronene
text:
The drawing is coronene (C24H12): a central six-membered ring fused to six outer six-membered rings. That gives 12 peripheral CH carbons and 12 quaternary carbons, 6 in the central ring and 6 outer fusion carbons.

I wrote the SMILES in aromatic form and checked it atom by atom. The 24 atoms are 12 CH and 12 quaternary. Atoms 19–24 form the central ring, and each is bonded to one of the outer fusion carbons (atoms 18, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15). The Kekulé structure shown in the image is one valid resonance form of this aromatic system.

SMILES: c1cc2ccc3ccc4ccc5ccc6ccc1c7c2c3c4c5c67

name: Corticosterone
text:
The drawing is a steroid skeleton (four fused rings) with these features:

- a 4-en-3-one in ring A (C=C conjugated with a ketone)
- a methyl on the A/B ring fusion carbon (C10) and another on C13, both drawn as wedges
- a hydroxyl on C11, drawn as a wedge
- a –C(=O)CH2OH side chain on C17, drawn as a wedge
- ring-fusion hydrogens: C8 wedge (up), C9 hashed (down) and C14 hashed (down)

This is corticosterone, a natural 11β-hydroxy corticosteroid. I took the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the standard corticosterone entry and checked it against the wedges and hashes in the image. I did not rederive each @/@@ label from the drawing atom by atom.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@H]4C(=O)CO)C)O

name: Cortisol
text:
The drawing matches cortisol (hydrocortisone), and I wrote the SMILES from the known structure rather than assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes independently.

- **Ring A:** an enone, with a C=C conjugated to the ring ketone (C=O) on the right.
- **Angular methyls:** wedged methyls at C10 and C13.
- **C11:** a wedged OH.
- **C17:** a hashed OH, with a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** H at C8 is wedged, and H at C9 and H at C14 are hashed.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(C(=O)CO)O)C)O

name: Cortisone
text:
The drawing is the steroid cortisone (17,21-dihydroxypregn-4-ene-3,11,20-trione). I wrote the SMILES from the structure as follows:

- **Ring A:** a ketone at C3 conjugated with the C4=C5 double bond, with a wedged methyl on C10.
- **Ring C:** a ketone at C11.
- **Ring D:** a hashed OH on C17, which also carries the C(=O)CH2OH side chain, and a wedged methyl on C13.
- **Ring junction hydrogens:** wedged H on C8, hashed H on C9, hashed H on C14.

This corresponds to the natural cortisone configuration (8S, 9S, 10R, 13S, 14S, 17R). I took the stereo descriptors from my recollection of the standard cortisone SMILES rather than deriving each one from the wedges, so they are matched to the known natural configuration, not independently verified against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2C(=O)C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(C(=O)CO)O)C

name: Coumatetralyl
text:
The drawing shows a 4-hydroxycoumarin core bearing a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalen-1-yl group at C3. This is the structure of coumatetralyl.

**Coumarin part.** A benzene ring is fused to a pyranone ring. The ring oxygen connects to the lactone carbonyl (C=O). Next to the carbonyl is C3, which is double-bonded to C4, and C4 carries the OH. C4 is bonded to the aromatic carbon of the benzo ring.

**Tetralin part.** The CH attached to C3 is bonded to two carbons: one is an aromatic ring-fusion carbon, and the other starts a CH2–CH2–CH2 chain. That chain runs to the second aromatic ring-fusion carbon, which completes the saturated ring.

**Stereochemistry.** The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: OC1=C(C2CCCc3ccccc23)C(=O)Oc2ccccc12

name: Colistin
text:
I read the drawing as a polymyxin-like lipopeptide: a 6-methyloctanoyl chain on an acyclic tail of Dab–Thr–Dab, joined to a macrocyclic peptide ring. The stereo marks come from the wedges and hashes at each stereocentre.

**Acyclic tail**
- The chain is 6-methyloctanoyl: CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH2C(=O)–, attached to an NH.
- Next come Dab (a side chain CH2CH2NH2), then Thr (CH(OH)CH3), then another Dab.
- The last Dab NH attaches to the ring carbon drawn with a hashed bond.

**Macrocycle** (traced around the ring from the hashed-bond CH)
- The ring contains two plain CH2 groups, labelled "C" in the drawing, in place of a Dab side chain.
- Going round: CH (hashed N) → CH2 → CH2 → NH → C(=O) → Thr (OH-bearing side chain) → Dab → Dab → Leu → Leu → Dab → C(=O) back to the starting CH.
- The ring closure is written as `N[C@H]1…NC1=O`.

**Stereochemistry**
- Each stereocentre was assigned from its wedge or hash with the implicit hydrogen placed opposite the wedge.
- Most centres come out as L-amino acid configuration.
- The Leu next to the Dab on the ring's lower side comes out as the D form, because its isobutyl bond is hashed.

I did not run the SMILES through a parser, so validity is checked by hand only.

SMILES: CCC(C)CCCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCN)C(=O)N[C@H]1CCNC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC1=O

name: Creatine
text:
The drawing shows creatine, read as follows:

- A carboxylic acid group, HO–C(=O)–, is on the left.
- It is attached to a CH2 carbon.
- The CH2 is bonded to a nitrogen that also carries a methyl group.
- That nitrogen is bonded to a guanidine carbon, which has a double bond to NH and a single bond to NH2.

All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN(CC(=O)O)C(=N)N

name: Colistin A
text:
I read the drawing as a lipopeptide of the polymyxin/colistin type: a cyclic heptapeptide ring carrying a tripeptide side chain acylated by a 6-methyloctanoyl group.

**Fatty acid.** The acyl group is 6-methyloctanoyl: C=O, four CH2 groups, then CH(CH3)CH2CH3. The methyl wedge makes the branch carbon S.

**Linear part.** Reading from the acyl group, the residues are Dab, Thr, Dab. Each Dab carries a CH2CH2NH2 side chain, and each Thr carries CH(OH)CH3. Each Dab α-carbon is S (L). Each Thr is α-S, β-R (L).

**Ring.** The third residue, a Dab, is the branch point. Its side chain, written CH2–CH2–NH in the drawing (the two carbons labelled "C"), closes the ring onto the C-terminal Thr carbonyl. Going round the ring from that Dab, the residues are:

- Dab (L)
- Leu (D, R)
- Leu (L)
- Dab (L)
- Dab (L)
- Thr (L)

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge/hash pattern and the CIP priorities, then converted to @/@@ with the neighbour order of the SMILES.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)CCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCN)C(=O)N[C@H]1CCNC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC1=O

name: Cositecan
text:
This is 7-(2-trimethylsilylethyl)camptothecin (karenitecin). The ring system is the camptothecin pentacycle. The drawing shows the following:

- A quinoline unit fused to the pyrrolo ring.
- A pyridone ring carrying the ring C=O attached to N.
- A lactone containing a quaternary carbon, which bears an ethyl group and a wedged OH.
- A –CH2CH2–Si(CH3)3 chain on the quinoline carbon next to the benzo ring, which is the 7-position.

For the stereocentre, I used the camptothecin SMILES as a template and added the silylethyl substituent. I then checked the wedge geometry against the drawing. Viewed from the wedged OH, the ethyl, the aromatic carbon and the lactone carbonyl carbon run clockwise. This matches `@@` in the SMILES order used.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(C2=C(COC1=O)C(=O)N3CC4=C(CC[Si](C)(C)C)C5=CC=CC=C5N=C4C3=C2)O

name: Crenolanib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Oxetane:** an O and three carbons form a four-membered ring. The quaternary ring carbon carries a methyl and a CH2–O– substituent.
- **Linker:** the CH2–O connects to the benzimidazole benzene ring.
- **Benzimidazole:** N1 is attached to the quinoline C2, and N3 is the pyridine-type nitrogen drawn with a double bond to C2 of the imidazole.
- **Quinoline:** C2 is bonded to the benzimidazole N1. The quinoline nitrogen sits next to the fused ring carbon, and C8 carries the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen is bonded to quinoline C8, and the 4-position carries NH2.

Benzimidazole substitution: the benzene ring carbon bearing the O sits next to the CH that is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N3 (the lower fusion carbon, attached to N=). From the coordinates, the O-bearing carbon at (510,785) is bonded to (577,872), which is bonded to the fusion carbon (688,857) that is attached to N3 (the N at the bottom). So the O is at position 5 of the benzimidazole, which is para to the carbon attached to N1.

SMILES, written from the oxetane outward:
CC1(COc2ccc3c(c2)ncn3-c2ccc3cccc(N4CCC(N)CC4)c3n2)COC1

Check of the benzimidazole: c2ccc3c(c2)ncn3 has the O-bearing c2, then c, c, then c3 (the fusion carbon bonded to n3, which is N1 and carries the quinoline). The next atom c(c2) is the other fusion carbon, bonded to the CH that closes to c2, and it connects to n (N3). So the O-bearing carbon is bonded to the CH that is adjacent to the fusion carbon bearing N3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC1(COc2ccc3c(c2)ncn3-c2ccc3cccc(N4CCC(N)CC4)c3n2)COC1

name: Crisaborole
text:
The drawing shows a benzoxaborole (a 1-hydroxy-1,3-dihydro-2,1-benzoxaborole) carrying a 4-cyanophenoxy group, similar to crisaborole.

**Oxaborole ring.** B carries an OH and is bonded to the ring O and to an aromatic carbon. The ring O connects to a CH2, and the CH2 connects to the other fused aromatic carbon.

**Fused benzene ring.** Reading around the ring, the vertices are:
- C1 (394,732), bonded to B
- C2 (403,584)
- C3 (537,519)
- C4 (659,601), bonded to the ether O
- C5 (651,749)
- C6 (517,815), bonded to the CH2

**Substituent.** The ether O links C4 to a para-substituted phenyl ring bearing a C≡N group.

**Position check.** C1 (B-bearing) is bonded to C2 and C6. C6 (CH2-bearing) is bonded to C5. C4 (O-bearing) is bonded to C3 and C5. So the O sits on the carbon that is meta to C6 and para to C1. In crisaborole, the 4-cyanophenoxy group is at position 5 of the benzoxaborole. Position 5 is para to C7a, which is the carbon bonded to B (C7a–B–O1–C3–C3a). That matches this drawing.

**SMILES.** Starting from the hydroxyl: OB1OCc2cc(Oc3ccc(C#N)cc3)ccc21

Checking the ring closures: B1, O, CH2, then c2 (C6), then c (C5), then c(OAr) (C4), then c (C3), c (C2), and c21 (C1, closing to the aromatic ring start and to B). This is consistent with the connectivity above.

SMILES: OB1OCc2cc(Oc3ccc(C#N)cc3)ccc21

name: Cromolyn
text:
This is cromolyn (cromoglicic acid). Each half is a chromone: a 4-oxo-4H-chromene-2-carboxylic acid with the ether oxygen attached at C5. The two halves are joined through O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O.

Reading the left half: the carboxylic acid carbon is attached to C2, which is double-bonded to C3. C3 connects to C4 (C=O), then to C4a, which is part of the benzene ring. C5 carries the ether oxygen, C8a is bonded to the ring oxygen O1, and O1 closes back to C2.

SMILES for one half: OC(=O)C1=CC(=O)c2c(OC...)cccc2O1

Full molecule: OC(=O)C1=CC(=O)c2c(OCC(O)COc3cccc4OC(C(=O)O)=CC(=O)c34)cccc2O1

Check on the second half: c3cccc4OC(C(=O)O)=CC(=O)c34. Atom c3 is C5, bonded to the ether oxygen. Then c, c, c are C6, C7 and C8, and c4 is C8a, which bears O1. O1 is bonded to C2 (bearing COOH), which is double-bonded to C3. C3 connects to C4 (C=O), which connects to c34, the C4a atom that closes both rings. This is correct.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1=CC(=O)c2c(OCC(O)COc3cccc4OC(C(=O)O)=CC(=O)c34)cccc2O1

name: Crystal Violet
text:
The drawing is a triarylmethane dye with the central carbon double-bonded to a quinoid ring. It looks like crystal violet minus one dimethylamino group, which is the structure of malachite green chloride.

**Central carbon:** it carries two aryl groups and a double bond to the third ring. The upper-left ring is a para-substituted benzene bearing N(CH3)2. The right ring is a para-substituted benzene bearing N(CH3)2. The bottom ring is quinoid, with the central carbon double-bonded to one ring carbon and a C=N+(CH3)2 at the para position.

**Bottom ring:** the central carbon is double-bonded to the ring carbon at (490,885). The ring then alternates as follows:
- (490,885) to (568,1020) is a single bond.
- (568,1020) to (490,1155) is a double bond.
- (490,1155) to (335,1155) is a single bond.
- (335,1155) to N+ is a double bond.
- (335,1155) to (257,1020) is a single bond.
- (257,1020) to (335,885) is a double bond.
- (335,885) to (490,885) is a single bond.

**SMILES:** C(=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1)(c1ccc(N(C)C)cc1)c1ccc(N(C)C)cc1.[Cl-]

SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccc(N(C)C)cc1)=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1.[Cl-]

name: Cupric acetate
text:
The image shows two acetate anions and one copper(II) cation, drawn as separate fragments.

- Each acetate is a methyl group bonded to a carbon that has a double bond to O and a single bond to O⁻. That gives CC(=O)[O-].
- The copper is labelled Cu with a 2+ charge and a radical dot, written [Cu+2] with the dot. The dot most likely arises from how the SMILES was generated, as in the form `[Cu++]`, so I wrote the dot as a separator between fragments. The charge is balanced: 2 × (−1) + 2 = 0.

SMILES: CC(=O)[O-].CC(=O)[O-].[Cu+2]

name: Crizotinib
text:
The molecule has the connectivity of crizotinib, and the hashed methyl on the stereocentre gives the (R) configuration. I read it as follows:

- **Left:** a piperidine ring (NH at the bottom left) is attached through its 4-position to N1 of a pyrazole.
- **Middle:** the pyrazole C4 is bonded to C5 of a pyridine ring. That pyridine carries an NH2 on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen, and an ether oxygen on the neighbouring carbon.
- **Right:** the ether oxygen is bonded to a CH carbon bearing a hashed methyl. That carbon is also bonded to a benzene ring, which has Cl on both ortho positions and F on the ring carbon next to one of the Cl-bearing carbons.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are O > aryl carbon > CH3 > H. The methyl is hashed (pointing back), so H points toward the viewer. Going O → aryl → CH3 on the page appears counterclockwise, which reverses to clockwise once H is placed at the back, so the centre is R. Written as `C[C@@H](O...)c1...`, this gives R.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Oc1cc(cnc1N)-c1cnn(c1)C1CCNCC1)c1c(Cl)ccc(F)c1Cl

name: Cupric Chloride
text:
The image shows a copper atom (Cu) in the centre with a single bond to a chlorine atom (Cl) on each side. No charges are drawn, so this is copper(II) chloride written as covalent bonds.

SMILES: Cl[Cu]Cl

name: Cyclizine
text:
The drawing shows a benzhydryl group (a CH carbon bearing two phenyl rings) bonded to one nitrogen of a piperazine ring. The other piperazine nitrogen carries a methyl group. This is cyclizine.

- Two phenyl rings, each drawn with alternating double bonds, attach to a single central carbon.
- That central carbon is bonded to N.
- The piperazine ring has two nitrogens separated by two CH2 groups on each side.
- The second nitrogen bears the CH3.
- There are no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Cyclobenzaprine
text:
This is cyclobenzaprine: a dibenzo[a,d]cycloheptene core carrying an exocyclic =CH–CH2–CH2–N(CH3)2 chain.

**Reading the drawing**
- The nitrogen carries two methyl groups and connects to a CH2–CH2–CH= chain.
- That chain ends in a double bond to the ring carbon at about (893, 838).
- This ring carbon is bonded to the top benzene ring carbon at (836, 648) and to the bottom benzene ring carbon at (1080, 911).
- The top benzene ring runs through (836, 648), (948, 483), (862, 303), (664, 288), (551, 453) and (637, 633).
- A CH=CH unit runs from (948, 483) through (1147, 468) and (1282, 615) to (1252, 812).
- The bottom benzene ring contains (1252, 812), (1080, 911), (1080, 1111), (1252, 1211) and (1424, 1111).

**Stereochemistry**
The exocyclic double bond has two different substituents on the chain carbon (H and CH2) and two ring substituents on the other carbon. These are the two aryl groups, which are different. The drawing shows the chain going down-left from the double bond. I will leave the stereo off.

**SMILES**
CN(C)CCC=C1c2ccccc2C=Cc2ccccc12

SMILES: CN(C)CCC=C1c2ccccc2C=Cc2ccccc12

name: Cycloguanil
text:
The drawing is a cycloguanil-type dihydrotriazine.

**Ring atoms.** The six-membered ring contains:
- C(NH2), at the top right of the ring, bonded to N1.
- N1, the nitrogen bearing the aryl group.
- C(CH3)2, the quaternary carbon.
- N=, at the bottom left.
- C(NH2), at the left.
- N=, at the top left.

**Bonds.**
- The top-left N has a double bond to the top-right C (the one bearing NH2).
- The bottom-left N has a double bond to the left C (the one bearing the other NH2).
- The N1 nitrogen carries the 4-chlorophenyl group.

**SMILES.** Starting at the top-right carbon: NC1=NC(N)=NC(C)(C)N1c1ccc(Cl)cc1.

**Check.**
- C1 is bonded to NH2, double-bonded to N, then goes to C(N), which is double-bonded to the next N.
- That N connects to CMe2, which connects to N1, which closes back to C1.
- Atom order around the ring: C1(NH2)=N–C(NH2)=N–C(Me)2–N1(Ar). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC1=NC(N)=NC(C)(C)N1c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Cyclohexane-D12
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered carbon ring (cyclohexane). Each ring carbon carries two substituents, and every substituent is labelled ²H (deuterium). That gives 12 deuteriums in total, so the molecule is cyclohexane-d12. All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included.

Each ring carbon is written as [2H]C([2H]) in the SMILES, which keeps the ring closure on the carbon atoms.

SMILES: [2H]C1([2H])C([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])C1([2H])[2H]

name: Complestatin
text:
I read the drawing as a vancomycin/teicoplanin-like glycopeptide: a macrocyclic peptide core with a central ring, a 6-aryl-indole and a diaryl ether, plus a 3,5-dichloro-4-hydroxyphenylglyoxylamide cap and a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine tail. The SMILES below follows that reading, with two caveats.

**Caveats**
- Near the left-hand stereocentre, the drawing shows an N–O line that would give the oxygen three bonds. I treated it as a drawing artefact and wrote an ordinary secondary amide NH there, so the N–O bond is not in the SMILES.
- I assigned the five stereocentres by hand from the wedge and hash bonds, so a chirality tag could be wrong.

**Fragments I read from the drawing**
- **Tail:** a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine (HOOC–CH(Ar)–NH–) acylated by the first peptide carbonyl.
- **Ether ring:** a para-substituted phenyl joined through CH₂ to the first stereocentre and through an ether oxygen to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** a benzene bearing the ether oxygen, an OH, the indole-linked aryl bond, and the CH(NH)–C(=O) side chain.
- **Indole:** attached through its 6-position to the central ring, with CH₂ at its 3-position.
- **Peptide chain:** two further amino-acid residues each carry a 3,5-dichloro-4-hydroxyphenyl group.
- **Cap:** the 3,5-dichloro-4-hydroxyphenylglyoxylamide on the indolylalanine nitrogen.

SMILES: OC(=O)C(c1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@@H]2Cc3ccc(cc3)Oc4c(O)c(cc9c4)-c5ccc6c(c5)[nH]cc6C[C@@H](NC(=O)C(=O)c7cc(Cl)c(O)c(Cl)c7)C(=O)N[C@@H](c8cc(Cl)c(O)c(Cl)c8)C(=O)N[C@@H]9C(=O)N[C@H](c%10cc(Cl)c(O)c(Cl)c%10)C(=O)N2

name: Cyclophosphamide
text:
The drawing shows cyclophosphamide.

- **Ring:** a six-membered ring made of P, O, CH2, CH2, CH2 and NH. The O is bonded to P and to the first CH2, and the NH is bonded to P and to the third CH2.
- **P substituents:** a P=O double bond and an exocyclic N atom.
- **Exocyclic N:** carries two CH2CH2Cl chains.
- **Stereochemistry:** P is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is written.

SMILES: ClCCN(CCCl)P1(=O)NCCCO1

name: Cyclopropane
text:
The image shows a plain triangle with three vertices and no labels, so it is a cyclopropane ring.

SMILES: C1CC1

name: Cycloplatam
text:
The image shows three separate components, so the SMILES is written as three dot-separated fragments.

1. **Malate dianion.** The chain is O=C([O-])C(O)CC(=O)[O-]. The left carboxylate carbon is bonded to =O and O⁻, then to CH(OH), then CH2, then the right carboxylate C(=O)[O-]. No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is given.

2. **Cyclopentylamine.** The ring is NC1CCCC1, drawn as H2N attached to a five-membered carbocycle.

3. **Platinum ammine fragment.** This is drawn as NH3 next to Pt²⁺, written [NH3][Pt+2]. The NH3 is shown without a charge and the Pt carries 2+, so I wrote it as a bond between N and Pt: [NH3][Pt+2].

The charges balance: two O⁻ and one Pt²⁺.

SMILES: O=C([O-])C(O)CC(=O)[O-].NC1CCCC1.[NH3][Pt+2]

name: Cryptophycin 52
text:
I read the structure as a 16-membered macrocyclic depsipeptide, a cryptophycin-type scaffold. This is my reading of the drawing, with the stereocentres assigned from the wedges and hashes.

**Macrocycle, traced clockwise from the isobutyl-bearing carbon**
1. The ring starts at a CH carrying an isobutyl group (drawn with a hashed bond) and bonded to a ring oxygen.
2. That oxygen links to an ester C(=O), then to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyls.
3. Next comes a CH2, then an NH, then an amide C(=O).
4. The following CH has a wedged CH2 leading to a 3-chloro-4-methoxyphenyl ring.
5. It is bonded to a second NH, which leads to a C(=O) and then a trans CH=CH, since the C=O and CH2 substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond.
6. A CH2 follows, then a CH bearing a wedged bond and the second ring oxygen.
7. That oxygen connects to the C(=O) bonded back to the first CH, closing the ring.

**Side chain on the oxygen-bearing CH**
- A wedged-methyl CH is attached to a trans-disubstituted epoxide.
- The epoxide carries a phenyl group on its far carbon, drawn with a wedge.

**Stereo**
I assigned each centre's @/@@ from the 2D positions of its neighbours and the wedge or hash.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@@H]1OC(=O)C(C)(C)CNC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccc(OC)c(Cl)c2)NC(=O)/C=C/C[C@H](OC1=O)[C@H](C)[C@H]1O[C@@H]1c1ccccc1

name: Cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]) hydrate
text:
The drawing is a cucurbituril macrocycle. I counted 14 carbonyl oxygens, which means 7 glycoluril units, so this is cucurbit[7]uril, C42H42N28O14. Adjacent glycoluril units are joined by two CH2 bridges, one at each portal, and the 7 units close into a ring. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

I built the SMILES as seven glycoluril fragments written separated by dots. Each fragment has a top carbonyl ring and a bottom carbonyl ring that share the CH–CH bond. The CH2 bridges between neighbouring units, and the seventh-to-first closure, are made with ring-closure labels (%11–%17 for the top bridges, %21–%27 for the bottom bridges).

I did not run this through a SMILES parser. I checked by hand that every ring-closure label is opened once and closed once, and that the atom counts match C42H42N28O14.

SMILES: N1%17C(=O)N(C%11)C2C1N%27C(=O)N2C%21.N1%11C(=O)N(C%12)C2C1N%21C(=O)N2C%22.N1%12C(=O)N(C%13)C2C1N%22C(=O)N2C%23.N1%13C(=O)N(C%14)C2C1N%23C(=O)N2C%24.N1%14C(=O)N(C%15)C2C1N%24C(=O)N2C%25.N1%15C(=O)N(C%16)C2C1N%25C(=O)N2C%26.N1%16C(=O)N(C%17)C2C1N%26C(=O)N2C%27

name: Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows cyproheptadine hydrochloride.

- Two benzene rings are fused to a seven-membered ring. The seven-membered ring contains a CH=CH unit, with each alkene carbon bonded to one of the benzene rings.
- The seventh ring carbon is bonded to the two benzene rings and carries an exocyclic double bond to C4 of the piperidine ring.
- The piperidine nitrogen bears a methyl group.
- HCl is drawn as a separate component.

SMILES for the free base: CN1CCC(CC1)=C1c2ccccc2C=Cc2ccccc12

Adding HCl as a separate component gives the final SMILES.

SMILES: Cl.CN1CCC(CC1)=C1c2ccccc2C=Cc2ccccc12

name: Cycloserine
text:
The drawing shows cycloserine (4-amino-1,2-oxazolidin-3-one), a five-membered ring with these atoms:

- The ring runs O1–N2(H)–C3(=O)–C4–C5, with C5 bonded back to O1.
- C3 carries a C=O (drawn as a double bond to the labelled O at top right).
- C4 carries an NH2 group and is the only stereocentre.

The NH2 bond at C4 is drawn as a hashed wedge, so NH2 points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

Assigning the configuration at C4:

- The CIP priorities are N > C3 (O,O,N) > C5 (O,H,H) > H.
- In the drawing, N is at lower right, C3 is above and C5 is at lower left, so N → C3 → C5 runs counterclockwise.
- The H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R.

The SMILES N[C@@H]1CONC1=O, read from the N atom, gives the same R assignment, so it matches the drawing (this is D-cycloserine).

SMILES: N[C@@H]1CONC1=O

name: Cysteamine
text:
The drawing shows an HS group bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a second CH2, which is bonded to NH2. That is a two-carbon chain with a thiol on one end and an amine on the other (2-aminoethanethiol, also called cysteamine). It has no rings, charges, or stereochemistry.

SMILES: SCCN

name: Cyclosporin A
text:
I read this as cyclosporin A, a cyclic undecapeptide. I matched the ring to its known residue order rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges. The stereo descriptors therefore come from the known SMILES for cyclosporin A, and I did not re-derive each one from the drawing.

Going round the ring from the aminobutyric acid residue, the drawing shows:
1. Abu (the ethyl-substituted residue at the bottom).
2. Sarcosine, where the labelled "C" is just the explicit CH2 of N-methylglycine.
3. N-Me-Leu.
4. Val (NH).
5. N-Me-Leu.
6. Ala (NH).
7. D-Ala (NH, drawn with a wedge methyl).
8. N-Me-Leu.
9. N-Me-Leu.
10. N-Me-Val.
11. MeBmt, the hydroxylated residue with the (E)-but-2-enyl side chain, N-methylated and closing the ring back to Abu.

I did not fully re-check the SMILES for valid syntax and atom counts.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1C(=O)N(CC(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)N1)[C@@H]([C@H](C)C/C=C/C)O)C)C(C)C)C)CC(C)C)C)CC(C)C)C)C)C)CC(C)C)C)C(C)C)CC(C)C)C

name: (-)-Cystine
text:
The drawing is cystine: two cysteine units joined through an S–S bond. Each half has an H2N–CH(CH2–S)–COOH core, and both amine bonds are drawn as hashed wedges.

**Stereochemistry (left centre):**
- The hashed NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- The CIP priorities are NH2 > CH2S > COOH > H.
- Seen from the front, NH2 (bottom), CH2S (upper right) and COOH (upper left) run counterclockwise.
- Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R.

**Right centre:** the drawing is symmetric under a 180° rotation, so this centre is also R. The molecule is therefore (R,R), which is L-cystine.

**SMILES check:** L-cysteine is N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O. Writing the second half from the sulfur side swaps the order of the neighbours, which turns @@ into @. This gives the string below.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CSSC[C@H](N)C(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Cythioate
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring.

- One substituent is O–P(=S)(OC)OC, a dimethyl thiophosphate ester. P carries a double bond to S, two OCH3 groups, and an O link to the ring.
- The other substituent is a primary sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)NH2.

SMILES: COP(=S)(OC)Oc1ccc(cc1)S(N)(=O)=O

name: Cytarabine
text:
The drawing shows a cytosine base joined through N1 to a furanose ring, which is an arabinofuranosyl cytosine (cytarabine, ara-C).

**Base:** A six-membered ring with N1 (attached to the sugar), C2 as C=O, N3, C4 bearing NH2, and a C5=C6 double bond. This is cytosine.

**Sugar:** A five-membered ring made of O4' and C1' to C4'. C4' carries a CH2OH group, and C2' and C3' each carry an OH.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes:**
- C1': the bond to the base N is a wedge (up).
- C2': the OH is a wedge (up), on the same face as the base. In ribo-cytidine the 2'-OH would be on the opposite face, so this makes it the arabino isomer.
- C3': the OH is hashed (down).
- C4': the CH2OH is a wedge (up).

I derived the C1' configuration from the drawn geometry and took the C3' and C4' descriptors from the standard cytidine SMILES, since both centres are drawn the same way as in cytidine. The C2' descriptor is the one that differs from cytidine.

SMILES: NC1=NC(=O)N(C=C1)[C@@H]1O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Cytisine
text:
I read the drawing as cytisine, a tricyclic skeleton with a 2-pyridone ring, a lactam N–CH2 bridge and a piperidine bearing an NH. The stereo comes from the two wedged hydrogens.

**Connectivity**
- The pyridone ring is O=C1–C=C–C=C2–N1. The carbonyl carbon is bonded to N, and the ring carries two C=C double bonds.
- The ring nitrogen N is bonded to a CH2, which leads to the stereocentre at the bottom (call it C_b).
- C_b is joined to a bridging CH2, which leads to the upper stereocentre (C_a).
- C_a is bonded to the pyridone carbon C2. This is the closure of ring 2 in the SMILES.
- C_a and C_b are also linked through CH2–NH–CH2 on the left, which closes the piperidine ring (ring closure 3 in the SMILES).

**Stereochemistry**
- Both hydrogens are drawn as wedges, toward the viewer.
- For C_b, I took the neighbours in SMILES order (N-side CH2, H, ring-closure CH2, bridge CH2). Viewed from the front, the three carbon neighbours run clockwise with H toward the viewer. That gives `[C@H]`.
- For C_a, I took the order (bridge CH2, H, pyridone carbon, CH2 toward NH). The three carbon neighbours run counterclockwise with H toward the viewer. That gives `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C1C=CC=C2N1C[C@H]3C[C@@H]2CNC3

name: Cyproterone Acetate
text:
I read the structure as cyproterone acetate. I derived the stereo marks from the wedges and hashes at each drawn stereocentre, but I did not independently check the final string against a reference.

**Skeleton**
- A steroid core with a 6-chloro substituent and a 4,6-diene-3-one system (C=C–C(Cl)=C conjugated through to the C=O).
- A cyclopropane fused across the 1,2-positions, drawn at the lower right.
- At C17, an acetoxy group (OC(=O)CH3) and an acetyl group (C(=O)CH3) on the same carbon.
- Two angular methyl groups, at C10 and C13.

**Stereochemistry**
- C17: acetoxy O on a hash.
- C13 and C10: methyls on wedges.
- C14 and C9: H on hashes.
- C8: H on a wedge.
- Both cyclopropane-fusion CH carbons (C1 and C2): H on wedges.

For each centre I took the drawn neighbours in SMILES order and assigned @ or @@ from the on-screen rotation, flipping for hashed bonds and for the permutation to the SMILES atom order.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[C@]1(C(C)=O)CC[C@H]2[C@@H]3C=C(Cl)C4=CC(=O)[C@@H]5C[C@@H]5[C@]4(C)[C@H]3CC[C@]12C

name: D-Fructose
text:
I read the ring as a six-membered pyranose: five carbons plus one ring oxygen. The anomeric carbon carries an OH and a CH2OH. It is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo. That makes the molecule a hexulopyranose (fructopyranose-type) with three stereocentres: the carbons next to the anomeric carbon and the ring CH2.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash and the neighbour order in the SMILES:

- **Ring carbon next to the CH2 (OH on a bold wedge):** `[C@@H]`
- **Middle ring carbon (OH on a bold wedge):** `[C@@H]`
- **Ring carbon next to the anomeric carbon (OH on a hashed bond):** `[C@@H]`

I wrote the SMILES starting from the CH2OH group and closing the ring at the anomeric carbon. I checked that it has the same atoms as the drawing: six carbons, the ring oxygen and four hydroxyl groups, plus the CH2OH oxygen.

SMILES: OCC1(O)OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: D-Galactose
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose (six-membered ring with one ring oxygen) carrying a CH2OH group and four OH groups.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring atoms are C1, O, C5, C4, C3 and C2.
- C1 (top) carries an OH drawn with a plain bond, so it gets no stereo label.
- C5 carries the CH2OH on a hashed bond.
- C4 and C3 each carry an OH on a hashed bond.
- C2 carries an OH on a wedge bond.

**Stereo assignment**
I wrote the SMILES in the order OC1O[C@H](CO)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O. For each stereocentre I took the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedge or hash, then worked out @ or @@ from the 2D coordinates. Each of C5, C4, C3 and C2 came out as @.

The SMILES is valid and accounts for all six ring atoms and every drawn substituent.

SMILES: OC1O[C@H](CO)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: D-Glucose
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose ring (five carbons plus one ring oxygen) carrying four OH groups and one CH2OH.

**Ring and substituents.** Going around the ring from the top left:
- The top-left carbon (C1) bears an OH drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- The next carbon down the left side (C2) bears an OH on a wedge.
- The bottom-left carbon (C3) bears an OH on a hash.
- The bottom-right carbon (C4) bears an OH on a wedge.
- The right carbon (C5) bears a CH2OH on a hash and is bonded to the ring oxygen at the top.

**Stereo assignment.** For each stereocentre I took the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedge or hash substituent. I then read the rotation of the other three neighbours from the 2D coordinates and converted to @ or @@ for the SMILES neighbour order. This gives:
- C5: `[C@H](CO)`
- C4: `[C@@H](O)`
- C3: `[C@H](O)`
- C2: `[C@H]1O`

The SMILES below is valid and accounts for every atom in the drawing: 6 ring atoms, 4 OH groups and 1 CH2OH.

SMILES: OC1O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Dabigatran
text:
This structure is dabigatran, and I read it region by region.

- **Amidine end:** a benzene ring carries C(=N)N (amidine) at one para position and NH–CH2 at the other.
- **Benzimidazole:** the CH2 attaches to C2 of the benzimidazole. N1 carries a methyl group, and the other ring nitrogen (N3) is the =N.
- **Amide:** the benzene ring of the benzimidazole carries a C(=O) group that bonds to a tertiary nitrogen. That nitrogen bears a 2-pyridyl group and a CH2CH2COOH chain.

The ring fusion follows the drawing. N1 (with methyl) attaches to the ring carbon at the top (c3a-type) of the fused benzene, and N3 attaches to the lower fusion carbon. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is the right-hand vertex of the benzene ring. Going around that ring: the fusion carbon next to N1, then the top-left CH, the top-right CH, the carbonyl-bearing C, the bottom CH, and the fusion carbon next to N3. The carbonyl carbon is therefore para to the N1-side fusion carbon, which matches dabigatran.

SMILES: CN1C(CNc2ccc(C(N)=N)cc2)=Nc2cc(C(=O)N(CCC(=O)O)c3ccccn3)ccc21

name: D-Phenylalanine, (2S)-N-((2R)-2-(2-(3-aminopropyl)phenoxy)propyl)-2-cyclopropylglycyl-N-methyl-D-alanyl-4-fluoro-, (3->1)-lactam
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle and wrote it as one SMILES, tracing the ring from the N-methyl amide nitrogen around the drawing.

**Ring sequence**
1. N-methyl amide nitrogen, then its C(=O).
2. The CH bearing the cyclopropyl group.
3. NH, then CH2.
4. The CH(CH3) carbon, then the ether O.
5. An ortho-disubstituted benzene ring.
6. Three CH2 groups, then NH.
7. C(=O), then the CH bearing a 4-fluorobenzyl group.
8. NH, then C(=O).
9. The CH(CH3) carbon, which closes the ring at the N-methyl nitrogen.

**Stereocentres**
I assigned each from its wedge or hash and the neighbour arrangement in the drawing. There are four, and all are marked by wedges or hashes:
- The alanine-type CH(CH3) next to the N-methyl nitrogen has a wedged methyl.
- The cyclopropyl-bearing CH has a hashed bond to the cyclopropyl.
- The CH(CH3)–O carbon has a wedged methyl.
- The CH bearing the 4-fluorobenzyl group has a wedged CH2.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)[C@H](C2CC2)NC[C@@H](C)Oc2ccccc2CCCNC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccc(F)cc2)NC(=O)[C@H]1C

name: Cyclosporin C
text:
I read this as a cyclic undecapeptide of the cyclosporin type, with Thr at position 2 (cyclosporin C-like). The "C" label next to the N-methyl nitrogen on the lower edge is just the CH2 of sarcosine.

I traced the ring clockwise from the top D-Ala and found 11 residues:

1. D-Ala (wedged methyl)
2. L-Ala (hashed methyl)
3. N-Me-Leu
4. Val (the only N–H Val in the ring)
5. N-Me-Leu
6. Sar (the labelled "C")
7. Thr
8. MeBmt, the unsaturated hydroxy amino acid with the (E)-CH2–CH=CH–CH3 chain
9. N-Me-Val
10. N-Me-Leu
11. N-Me-Leu, which closes onto the D-Ala carbonyl

The peptide N–H groups are on D-Ala, L-Ala, Val and Thr, and the other residues carry N-methyl groups.

Stereochemistry follows the wedges and hashes. In the SMILES each α-carbon is written with its own carbonyl as the preceding atom, so the chirality tags follow that order. The MeBmt double bond is trans.

I did not run a validity check on the SMILES; I checked it by hand against the traced ring.

SMILES: O=C1[C@@H](C)NC(=O)[C@H](C)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)N(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)[C@H](C)C/C=C/C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)N1C

name: Dabigatran Ethyl Ester
text:
This is the dabigatran ethyl ester skeleton, with the amidine drawn as a free C(=N)N and the ester as an ethyl ester.

Reading the structure region by region:
- Ethyl ester: CH3CH2-O-C(=O)-CH2CH2-N.
- That nitrogen carries a 2-pyridyl group and an amide C(=O) linked to the benzimidazole at position 5.
- Benzimidazole: N1 bears a methyl and C2 bears CH2-NH-aryl. The other ring nitrogen, N3, is a plain =N.
- The aryl group is a para-substituted benzene bearing C(=N)N.

SMILES check, writing from the ethyl group onward:
CCOC(=O)CCN(c1ccccn1)C(=O)c1ccc2n(C)c(CNc3ccc(C(=N)N)cc3)nc2c1

Benzimidazole ring: c1 (C5, bearing the carbonyl), then c, c, c2 (C7a, attached to N1), n(C), c(CN...), n, c2 (C3a), c1 (C4). C5 is attached to C4 and C6. C4 is adjacent to C3a, which is bonded to N3. In the drawing, the carbonyl-bearing carbon is next to the lower ring carbon, which connects to the carbon bonded to N3. This matches the SMILES, where c1 (C5) connects through c1 at the end (C4) to c2 (C3a), which is bonded to the n of N3. The ring closes correctly.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCN(c1ccccn1)C(=O)c1ccc2n(C)c(CNc3ccc(C(=N)N)cc3)nc2c1

name: D-Ribose
text:
I read the drawing as a six-membered pyranose ring (five carbons and one ring oxygen) with four hydroxyl groups.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring runs C1–C2–C3–C4–C5–O, with C5 as a CH2 bonded to the ring oxygen.
- C1 is the anomeric carbon. It carries a plain-bond OH and is bonded to the ring oxygen, so it gets no stereo marking.
- C2, C3 and C4 each carry an OH drawn on a wedge bond.

**Stereo assignment** (hydrogen implicit and pointing away from the viewer)
- C4: O, C3, C5 run clockwise, so it is R.
- C3: O, C2, C4 run clockwise, so it is R.
- C2: O, C1, C3 run clockwise, so it is R.

I converted these into SMILES chirality marks, writing the atoms in the order OC1OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O. The three stereocentres come out as @@, @@ and @, and the wedge pattern matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC1OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Dabigatran Etexilate
text:
This drawing matches dabigatran etexilate, so I read it region by region and then wrote the SMILES.

**Hexyl carbamate end.** The chain has 6 carbons, drawn from the far-left methyl through the zigzag to the O. Reading the vertices: 75,885 → 108,835 → 170,840 → 203,793 → 265,797 → 297,747 → O. That is CH3, then 5 more carbons, so the chain is CCCCCC-O (hexyl). It is attached as O–C(=O)–NH–C(=N)–aryl, giving CCCCCCOC(=O)NC(=N)c1ccc(...)cc1.

**Linker and benzimidazole.** The aryl group carries NH–CH2 on the para position, and the CH2 sits on C2 of the benzimidazole. N1 carries a methyl. The benzimidazole is attached at C5 to C(=O)N.

**Amide end.** The amide nitrogen bears a pyridin-2-yl group and CH2CH2C(=O)OCH2CH3.

**Benzimidazole SMILES.** The ring is Cn1c(CNc2ccc(cc2)C(=N)NC(=O)OCCCCCC)nc2cc(ccc12)C(=O)N(CCC(=O)OCC)c1ccccn1.

**Ring-fusion check.** N1 (methylated) is bonded to C7a, which bonds to C7 and C6, then C5, which carries the carbonyl. C4 is next to C3a, which bonds to N3. In the drawing, the carbonyl-bearing carbon is bonded to the CH that is adjacent to C3a, which is C4. So the carbonyl carbon is C5, adjacent to C4 and C6, as written. In the SMILES, nc2cc(C(=O)...)ccc12 places c2 (C3a), then c (C4), then c(C=O) (C5), then c (C6), c (C7), c12 (C7a). This is consistent.

SMILES: CCCCCCOC(=O)NC(=N)c1ccc(NCc2nc3cc(C(=O)N(CCC(=O)OCC)c4ccccn4)ccc3n2C)cc1

name: Dabrafenib
text:
The drawing shows a molecule that matches dabrafenib's structure, but with the pyrimidine unsubstituted at C5. Dabrafenib itself has a 2-aminopyrimidin-4-yl group, so this reads as a des-methyl or related analog, and I wrote the SMILES from the drawing.

**Pyrimidine.** The ring runs N=C(NH2)–N=C(–thiazole)–C=C back to the first N. The 2-amino carbon sits between the two ring nitrogens. The ring carbon bearing the thiazole is bonded to the N. The remaining two ring carbons are CH=CH. SMILES: Nc1nccc(n1)-c...

**Thiazole.** S is bonded to C5, which carries the pyrimidine. C5=C4, and C4 carries the aryl group. C4 is bonded to N, N=C2, C2 carries the tert-butyl group, and C2 is bonded back to S.

**Central phenyl ring.** The carbon attached to the thiazole is next to a C–F carbon. That C–F carbon is next to the carbon bearing the NH. The ring is aromatic with six carbons.

**Sulfonamide.** The NH connects to S(=O)(=O), which connects to a 2,6-difluorophenyl ring.

Full SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1nc(c(s1)-c1ccnc(N)n1)-c1cccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2c(F)cccc2F)c1F

Checking the central ring: c1 (attached to the thiazole), then c, c, c, c(NHSO2), and c1F. Here c1F lies between the thiazole-bearing carbon and the NH-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1nc(c(s1)-c1ccnc(N)n1)-c1cccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2c(F)cccc2F)c1F

name: Dacomitinib
text:
The drawing shows a quinazoline core with three substituents, plus a piperidine on the side chain.

**Quinazoline core.** The pyrimidine ring is C4(=N3)–C2H=N1–C8a, fused to a benzene ring. The benzene ring carbons are C4a, C5 (H), C6 (bearing the amide NH), C7 (bearing OMe), C8 (H) and C8a.

**Substituents.**
- C4 carries an NH linked to a 3-chloro-4-fluorophenyl ring. In the drawing, the ring carbon bearing Cl sits next to the carbon bearing F.
- C6 carries NH–C(=O)–CH=CH–CH2–N(piperidine).
- C7 carries OCH3.

**Double-bond geometry.** The C=C is drawn between the carbon next to the carbonyl and the next carbon. The carbonyl carbon lies at the right, the CH2 at the left, and the two chain bonds run roughly horizontally on opposite sides of the double bond. This is trans (E).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Aniline side: Fc1ccc(Nc2ncnc3cc(OC)c(NC(=O)/C=C/CN4CCCCC4)cc23)cc1Cl
- In the aryl ring, the NH carbon is para to F, and Cl is adjacent to F and meta to N, which matches the drawing.
- The fused ring: c2 is C4, then n, c, n, c3 (C8a), then c (C8, H), c(OC) (C7), c(NHCO…) (C6), c (C5, H), and c23 (C4a). This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: Fc1ccc(Nc2ncnc3cc(OC)c(NC(=O)/C=C/CN4CCCCC4)cc23)cc1Cl

name: Cyanocobalamin
text:
This SMILES is my reading of the drawing, built ring by ring. I did not check it with software, and the stereocentres were assigned by hand from the wedges and hashes.

**What the drawing shows**
- It is a cyanocobalamin-type skeleton in which the cobalt is not bonded to the ring. It is drawn as a separate `Co2+` and a separate cyanide drawn as N≡C with a radical dot.
- The four corrin ring nitrogens are drawn as three imine nitrogens and one NH.
- The corrin has the following peripheral groups:
  - Two propionamide-type chains and some of the acetamide side chains are drawn as imidate anions, `C(=N)[O-]`, rather than as primary amides.
  - One of these chains is a plain propionamide that carries the aminopropanol linker.
  - The gem-dimethyl carbon is on the top-right ring.
  - Methyl groups sit on the quaternary carbons, and there are two bridging methyl-bearing carbons.
- The linker runs from the amide NH through `CH2–CH(CH3)–O–P(=O)(OH)–O` to the ribose 3′-oxygen. The ribose carries a 5-CH2OH, a 2-OH, and a 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazolium on C1′.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash. These are the ribose carbons, the linker CH(CH3)O carbon, and the corrin carbons carrying side chains or methyls.

SMILES: CC1=C2NC([C@@H](CCC(=N)[O-])[C@]2(C)CC(N)=O)=CC3=NC(=C(C)C4=N[C@@H]([C@@]5(C)[C@@](C)(CC(N)=O)[C@H](CCC(=N)[O-])C1=N5)[C@H](CC(N)=O)[C@@]4(C)CCC(=O)NC[C@@H](C)OP(=O)(O)O[C@@H]6[C@@H](CO)O[C@H]([n+]7c[nH]c8cc(C)c(C)cc78)[C@@H]6O)[C@@H](CCC(=N)[O-])C3(C)C.[Co+2].N#[C]

name: Dactinomycin
text:
This molecule is actinomycin D: a phenoxazinone chromophore carrying two identical cyclic pentapeptide lactones (Thr, D‑Val, Pro, Sar, N‑Me‑Val). I recognised it as that known natural product and wrote the SMILES from memory of its literature form, rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the image. I did not check the stereo descriptors atom by atom against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N(CC(=O)N([C@H](C(=O)O1)C(C)C)C)C)C(C)C)NC(=O)C3=C4C(=C(C=C3)C)OC5=C(C(=O)C(=C(C5=N4)C(=O)N[C@@H]6[C@H](OC(=O)[C@@H](N(C(=O)CN(C(=O)[C@@H]7CCCN7C(=O)[C@@H](NC6=O)C(C)C)C)C)C(C)C)C)N)C

name: Daclatasvir
text:
This structure is daclatasvir, a symmetric molecule built around a biphenyl core with two imidazole–proline–valine carbamate arms.

**Structure read from the drawing:**
- The central unit is a biphenyl with para linkages. Each outer para position carries an imidazole attached at its C4/C5 carbon, adjacent to the ring NH.
- The imidazole C2 of each arm is bonded to the C2 of a pyrrolidine ring. This carbon is drawn with a hashed bond.
- The pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by a valine unit. The valine α-carbon is drawn with a bold wedge to the NH.
- The valine NH carries a methyl carbamate (NHC(=O)OCH₃), and the valine side chain is isopropyl.

**Stereochemistry:** I checked the left valine centre from the wedge geometry and found it is S, the natural L configuration. I assumed the other three centres follow the same pattern, since the drawing is symmetric and the hash/wedge pattern matches daclatasvir. I then confirmed that each stereo tag in the SMILES gives S by working through the CIP priorities.

SMILES: COC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1c1ncc([nH]1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1cnc([nH]1)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)C

name: Dantrolene
text:
This structure is dantrolene, which has a hydantoin ring, an N–N=CH linker, a furan ring and a 4-nitrophenyl group.

**Hydantoin ring:** the five-membered ring contains CH2, N, C(=O), NH and C(=O). The ring N bears the N=C substituent. Going around the ring from the CH2 carbon: CH2 – N(N=) – C(=O) – NH – C(=O) – back to CH2.

**Linker and furan:** the substituent N is bonded to N=CH, and the CH is attached to the furan C2. The furan runs C2, C3, C4, C5 with O closing the ring. C5 carries the aryl group.

**Aryl group:** a benzene ring with a nitro group para to the furan attachment, drawn as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no explicit double-bond geometry, so I include none.

SMILES: O=C1CN(N=Cc2ccc(o2)-c2ccc(cc2)[N+](=O)[O-])C(=O)N1

name: Danofloxacin
text:
I read this as a fluoroquinolone (it matches danofloxacin) with a 2,5-diazabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane substituent.

- **Core:** A quinolone ring system. N1 carries a cyclopropyl group, C3 carries a COOH, C4 is C=O, and C6 carries F.
- **C7 substituent:** The C7 carbon is bonded to one nitrogen of the bicycle.
- **Bicycle:** A 2,5-diazabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane. One nitrogen carries a methyl group, and the other is bonded to the aromatic ring. The two bridgehead carbons each have a wedged H.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the two bridgehead centres from the wedged H atoms. Viewed from each H, the neighbours run counterclockwise (lower bridgehead) and clockwise (upper bridgehead) in the drawing. This gives `[C@@H]` for the lower bridgehead and `[C@H]` for the upper one in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: CN1C[C@@H]2C[C@H]1CN2c1cc2n(C3CC3)cc(C(=O)O)c(=O)c2cc1F

name: Danuglipron Tromethamine
text:
The structure is the GLP-1 agonist danuglipron drawn as its tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (tris) salt, with the two components written as separate fragments. I identified it from the drawing and checked the stereocentre against the known (S)-configuration of danuglipron.

Reading the main component region by region:
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with a nitrile and a fluorine, linked through a CH2–O ether to the 2-position of a pyridine.
- **Middle:** the pyridine's 6-position carries a piperidin-4-yl group, and the piperidine nitrogen is attached through a CH2 to C2 of a benzimidazole.
- **Right:** the benzimidazole N1 carries a CH2 group attached to an oxetan-2-yl ring. That oxetane carbon is the only stereocentre, drawn with a hashed bond, and it is the (S) centre. The benzimidazole also bears a carboxylic acid on its benzo ring.
- **Counter-component:** the top fragment is tris, a central carbon bearing NH2 and three CH2OH groups.

I wrote the stereocentre as `[C@@H]` and checked that the neighbour ordering in my SMILES is an even permutation of the known danuglipron SMILES, so it describes the same configuration.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(COc2cccc(n2)C2CCN(CC2)Cc2nc3ccc(C(=O)O)cc3n2C[C@@H]2CCO2)c(F)c1.NC(CO)(CO)CO

name: Dapansutrile
text:
The drawing shows a methyl group attached to a sulfur that carries two double-bonded oxygens (a sulfone). The sulfur then connects to a CH2, then another CH2, then a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen (a nitrile).

Atom check: CH3, S(=O)(=O), CH2, CH2, C≡N. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing. There are no stereo elements.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CCC#N

name: Dapivirine
text:
This is the NNRTI dapivirine scaffold: a pyrimidine with a 2,4,6-trimethylanilino group at C4 and a 4-cyanoanilino group at C2.

**Pyrimidine ring.** Going round the ring: the top-left carbon (CH) is bonded to the C bearing the mesityl-NH, which is bonded to the lower N, then to the C bearing the NH-aryl, then to the right N, then to the top-right CH.

**Mesityl ring.** The ring carbon attached to NH has methyl groups on both neighbouring carbons (one upper-left, one right). The para carbon, at the bottom, also carries a methyl. This gives a 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl group.

**Cyanophenyl ring.** The NH is attached to a benzene ring that carries a C≡N at the para position.

SMILES: Cc1cc(C)c(Nc2ccnc(Nc3ccc(C#N)cc3)n2)c(C)c1

SMILES: Cc1cc(C)c(Nc2ccnc(Nc3ccc(C#N)cc3)n2)c(C)c1

name: Danoprevir
Dapagliflozin
text:
This structure is dapagliflozin, and I read it as follows.

- **Left side:** an ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** a CH2 connects that ring to a second benzene ring.
- **Second ring:** it carries the Cl and, on the other side, the sugar ring.
- **Sugar ring:** a six-membered ring containing one oxygen (a C-aryl glucoside) with three ring OH groups and a CH2OH. The anomeric carbon is bonded directly to the aryl ring by a hashed bond.

I derived the anomeric carbon's chirality ([C@@H]) directly from the wedge/hash drawing. I did not re-derive the other four ring stereocentres from the drawing; I took them from the known configuration of dapagliflozin.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(Cc2cc([C@@H]3O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]3O)ccc2Cl)cc1

name: Dapsone
text:
The drawing shows dapsone (4,4'-diaminodiphenyl sulfone). Reading it region by region:

- **Centre:** a sulfur atom with two double-bonded oxygens, so a sulfonyl group.
- **Left and right:** a benzene ring on each side of the sulfur, each joined at one ring carbon.
- **Substituents:** each ring carries an NH2 at the position para to the sulfonyl attachment. The left NH2 is directly opposite the sulfur-bearing carbon, and so is the right one.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(N)cc1

name: Dalfopristin
text:
I read the structure as the dalfopristin-type macrocycle and assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes as drawn.

**Side chain:** a diethylaminoethyl group (Et2N–CH2CH2–) is attached to a sulfone (S(=O)(=O)), which sits on the pyrrolidine ring.

**Pyrrolidine ring:** the ring N is acylated by the oxazole C=O. The sulfonyl-bearing carbon is a hashed stereocentre. The adjacent α-carbon carries a hashed H and is bonded to the ester C(=O)–O.

**Macrocycle, from the ester O onward:**
1. The O-bearing CH carries an isopropyl group on a wedge.
2. Next is a CH(CH3) with the methyl on a wedge.
3. A trans CH=CH follows, then C(=O)–NH.
4. The NH is followed by CH2, then a trans CH=CH, then C(CH3)=CH. At this trisubstituted alkene the chain and the CH(OH) carbon are trans to each other.
5. Next is a CH(OH) with a hashed OH, then CH2, then a ketone C(=O), then CH2.
6. The CH2 leads to the oxazole C2. The ring runs C2=N–C4(=C5H–O), and C4 bears the C(=O) that closes onto the pyrrolidine N.

The SMILES was checked for ring closures and for the stereo tags against the wedge/hash drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCS(=O)(=O)[C@@H]1CCN2[C@H]1C(=O)O[C@H](C(C)C)[C@H](C)/C=C/C(=O)NC/C=C/C(C)=C/[C@@H](O)CC(=O)CC3=NC(=CO3)C2=O

name: Dapoxetine
text:
The image shows dapoxetine, (S)-N,N-dimethyl-3-(naphthalen-1-yloxy)-1-phenylpropan-1-amine.

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring is attached to a stereocentre carbon, which also carries an N(CH3)2 group.
- **Chain:** from the stereocentre, a CH2–CH2 chain runs to an oxygen. The bond to the first CH2 is drawn as a hashed wedge.
- **Right side:** the oxygen is bonded to the 1-position of a naphthalene ring system (two fused six-membered rings).
- **Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N, then the phenyl carbon, then the CH2, then H. The hashed CH2 points away and the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page, N (bottom), phenyl (upper left) and CH2 (upper right) run clockwise. Reversing this because H faces the viewer gives S, which is `[C@@H]` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: CN(C)[C@@H](CCOc1cccc2ccccc12)c1ccccc1

name: Darifenacin Hydrobromide
text:
The image shows darifenacin hydrobromide, read as follows:

- **Left:** a 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran, attached through its 5-position to a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Middle:** the chain ends on the nitrogen of a pyrrolidine ring.
- **Right:** pyrrolidine C3 carries a quaternary carbon bearing two phenyl groups and a primary amide, C(=O)NH2.
- **Salt:** HBr is drawn as a separate component.

The only stereo-marked atom is pyrrolidine C3. A wedge runs from C3 to the diphenyl carbon, so that bond points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away.

CIP priorities at C3 are:
1. the ring CH2 attached to N
2. the diphenyl quaternary carbon
3. the ring CH2 on the other side (C4)
4. H

On the page, going from the N-side CH2 to the quaternary carbon to C4 runs counterclockwise with H at the back, so the centre is S. This matches darifenacin, the (S) enantiomer.

For the SMILES, writing `[C@@H]1` with neighbour order (quaternary C, H, ring-closure CH2, C4) gives S.

SMILES: NC(=O)C(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCN(CCc2ccc3OCCc3c2)C1.Br

name: Darinaparsin
text:
I read this as the dimethylarsino–glutathione conjugate: an (CH3)2As group bonded through sulfur to the cysteine side chain of γ‑Glu‑Cys‑Gly.

- **Arsenic end:** an As atom carries two methyl groups and is bonded to S, which connects to a CH2.
- **Cysteine unit:** the CH2 is attached to the cysteine α‑carbon. Its NH is acylated by the glutamate side‑chain carbonyl, and its C(=O) forms an amide with the glycine NH.
- **Glycine unit:** NH–CH2–C(=O)OH.
- **Glutamate unit:** the side chain is C(=O)–CH2–CH2, ending at the α‑carbon, which bears NH2 (drawn hashed) and COOH.

For stereochemistry, I assigned each centre from the drawing:

- **Glutamate α‑carbon:** the hashed NH2 puts H toward the viewer. With priorities N > COOH > CH2, the sequence reads clockwise from the front, so the true configuration is reversed to counterclockwise. This is S, the L‑glutamate configuration.
- **Cysteine α‑carbon:** the hashed CH2 puts H toward the viewer. With priorities N > CH2S > C(=O) > H, the sequence reads counterclockwise from the front, so the true configuration is reversed to clockwise. This is R, matching natural glutathione.

I wrote the SMILES by taking the standard glutathione SMILES, which has these same two configurations, and attaching S–As(CH3)2 to the cysteine CH2.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS[As](C)C)C(=O)NCC(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Darunavir
text:
This structure is darunavir, and I wrote the SMILES from the known structure of that drug. I did not independently derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

The drawing contains these fragments:
- A bicyclic bis-tetrahydrofuran (hexahydrofuro[2,3-b]furan) ring system with three stereocentres, drawn with wedges and hashes.
- A carbamate (O–C(=O)–NH) linking that ring system to the chain.
- A chain carrying a benzyl group on the carbon next to the NH, then a hydroxyl-bearing stereocentre, then a CH2 attached to a tertiary nitrogen.
- That nitrogen carries an isobutyl group and a sulfonyl group.
- The sulfonyl group is attached to a 4-aminophenyl ring.

SMILES: CC(C)CN(C[C@H]([C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)O[C@H]2CO[C@@H]3[C@H]2CCO3)O)S(=O)(=O)c4ccc(N)cc4

name: Dasatinib
text:
This structure is dasatinib, and I read it region by region from the drawing.

- **Pyrimidine:** a methyl group sits on the carbon between the two ring nitrogens. The ring carbon at the top bears the piperazine nitrogen, the next ring carbon is CH, and the carbon at the bottom bears the NH linker.
- **Piperazine:** one nitrogen is attached to the pyrimidine and the other carries a CH2CH2OH chain.
- **Thiazole:** the NH links the pyrimidine to C2 of the thiazole. C2 is bonded to S and double-bonded to N, then N–CH=C, and C5 carries the carboxamide.
- **Amide and aryl ring:** C(=O)N is attached to a benzene ring that has Cl on one ortho carbon and CH3 on the other.

SMILES: Cc1nc(cc(n1)Nc1ncc(s1)C(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1Cl)N1CCN(CCO)CC1

name: Darolutamide
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then fixed the one stereocentre.

- **Left ring:** a pyrazole with a 1-hydroxyethyl group on the carbon next to the NH. The carbon next to the other ring nitrogen carries the amide C(=O). The hydroxyethyl carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Linker:** the amide NH is attached to a CH that bears a hashed methyl and a CH2. The CH2 leads to N1 of the second pyrazole.
- **Second pyrazole:** N1 is substituted by the CH2, and C3 (the carbon next to N2) carries the aryl ring.
- **Aryl ring:** a phenyl ring with a nitrile (C#N) para to the pyrazole attachment, and a chlorine ortho to the nitrile (meta to the pyrazole).

For the stereocentre, I ranked the substituents as N, then CH2 (which carries N), then CH3, then H. The methyl is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. N → CH2 → CH3 runs clockwise in the drawing, which reverses to counterclockwise with H toward the viewer. That gives S. In the SMILES, writing the neighbours in the order CH3, H, CH2, N corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Cn1ccc(-c2ccc(C#N)c(Cl)c2)n1)NC(=O)c1cc(C(C)O)[nH]n1

name: Dazoxiben
text:
The drawing shows three parts:

- **Imidazole:** a five-membered ring in which N1 carries the chain. N1 is bonded to C2, and C2 is double-bonded to N3. N3 is bonded to C4, which is double-bonded to C5, and C5 closes back to N1.
- **Linker:** N1 is joined to a CH2–CH2 chain, which ends at an ether oxygen bonded to the benzene ring.
- **Benzoic acid:** a para-substituted benzene ring carrying the ether oxygen on one side and a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) on the other.

Writing this out as SMILES gives OC(=O)c1ccc(OCCn2ccnc2)cc1.

Checking the imidazole ring closure: n2ccnc2 reads as N1, C5, C4, N3, C2, with C2 closing back to N1. In the drawing, N1 connects to C2, and C2 is double-bonded to N3. Both match, so the SMILES agrees with the picture.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(OCCn2ccnc2)cc1

name: Decabromodiphenyl ether
text:
The image shows two benzene rings joined by an ether oxygen, with bromine on every other ring position.

Left ring: the carbon attached to O has five other positions, and all five carry Br (the ortho positions at upper right and bottom, the meta positions at upper left and lower left, and the para position at the top). So each ring is a pentabromophenyl group.

Checking the left ring atoms: C1 (597,840) bears O; C2 (440,930) bears Br; C3 (284,840) bears Br; C4 (284,658) bears Br; C5 (440,570) bears Br; C6 (597,658) bears Br. That is 5 Br.

The right ring is the same: C1 (910,840) bears O; the others at (1067,930), (1223,840), (1223,658), (1067,570) and (910,658) all bear Br. That is 5 Br, so the molecule is decabromodiphenyl ether.

SMILES: Brc1c(Br)c(Br)c(Br)c(Br)c1Oc1c(Br)c(Br)c(Br)c(Br)c1Br

name: Daunorubicin
Decoquinate
text:
I read the molecule as an ethyl 4-oxo-1H-quinoline-3-carboxylate core carrying two alkoxy groups on the benzene ring.

- **Core:** a 4-quinolone with an N–H at position 1 and a ketone (C=O) at position 4.
- **Position 3:** an ethyl ester, C(=O)OCH2CH3.
- **Position 7:** an ethoxy group (O–CH2CH3), on the ring carbon next to the one bonded to the ring-fusion carbon that carries N–H.
- **Position 6:** an unbranched alkoxy chain. Counting the zigzag vertices from the free end up to the oxygen gives 10 carbons, so this is a decyloxy group.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCOc1cc2c(cc1OCC)[nH]cc(C(=O)OCC)c2=O

name: Deferasirox
text:
This structure is deferasirox: a 1,2,4-triazole ring carrying two 2-hydroxyphenyl groups and an N-aryl group, with a 4-carboxyphenyl on the ring nitrogen.

Triazole ring, read from the drawing:
- N1 (the right-hand N, at about 740,680) bears the carboxyphenyl group.
- N2 (the top N, at about 615,595) is bonded to N1 and double-bonded to C3 (at about 500,683).
- C3 carries the left 2-hydroxyphenyl group.
- N4 (the lower N, at about 550,820) is double-bonded to C5 (at about 695,818).
- C5 is bonded to N1 and carries the bottom 2-hydroxyphenyl group.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)n1nc(nc1-c1ccccc1O)-c1ccccc1O

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)n1nc(nc1-c1ccccc1O)-c1ccccc1O

name: Deferiprone
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring containing one nitrogen (the pyridin-4-one core).

Ring atoms, going around:
- N, bearing a methyl group.
- C2, bearing a methyl group, joined to C3 by a double bond.
- C3, bearing OH.
- C4, bearing the exocyclic C=O.
- C5 and C6, joined by a double bond, with C6 bonded back to N.

This is 3-hydroxy-1,2-dimethylpyridin-4(1H)-one (deferiprone).

SMILES: Cc1n(C)ccc(=O)c1O

Written in non-aromatic form, which matches the drawn bonds: CN1C=CC(=O)C(O)=C1C

SMILES: CN1C=CC(=O)C(O)=C1C

name: Deferoxamine
text:
Reading the structure from left to right:

1. H2N is attached to a chain of five CH2 groups, which ends at N(OH).
2. That N(OH) is acylated by C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O), a succinyl unit.
3. The succinyl unit is bonded to NH, then five CH2 groups, then N(OH).
4. The second N(OH) carries another succinyl unit, C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O).
5. That unit is bonded to NH, then five CH2 groups, then N(OH).
6. The last N(OH) is acetylated, C(=O)CH3.

Chain length check: from H2N, the vertices run N, then carbons at x=148, 192, 236, 280, 324 (five carbons), then N at 366. This gives five CH2 groups.

The middle chain runs from NH at 588, through carbons at 632, 676, 720, 764, 808, to N at 852. That is also five CH2 groups.

The right chain runs from NH at 1072, through carbons at 1116, 1160, 1204, 1248, 1292, to N at 1336. That is five CH2 groups as well.

SMILES: NCCCCCN(O)C(=O)CCC(=O)NCCCCCN(O)C(=O)CCC(=O)NCCCCCN(O)C(C)=O

name: Deflazacort
text:
The drawing shows deflazacort, the 21-acetate of an oxazoline-fused 11β-hydroxy-pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione steroid. I assigned the stereochemistry by matching it to the known natural configuration of deflazacort rather than deriving each centre from the wedges, so the @/@@ marks are the least certain part.

- **A ring:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with C=O at the right and a C=C–C=C pattern.
- **C10 and C13:** both carry methyl groups drawn with hashed bonds.
- **C11:** carries the OH.
- **D ring:** fused at C16/C17 to a 2-methyl-oxazoline, with N attached to C17 and O to C16.
- **C17 side chain:** C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH3, i.e. the 21-acetate.

SMILES: CC1=N[C@@]2([C@@H](O1)C[C@@H]3[C@@]2(C[C@@H]([C@H]4[C@H]3CCC5=CC(=O)C=C[C@]45C)O)C)C(=O)COC(=O)C

name: Daptomycin
text:
I read the drawing as a decanoyl-capped peptide: a cyclic depsipeptide ring with a three-residue tail. It matches the daptomycin type of structure, but I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the image rather than from memory.

**Tail, from the decanoyl end:**
- A decanoyl chain, counted as 10 carbons including the C=O.
- Trp, with the L configuration taken from its wedged CH2.
- Asn, which comes out as the D configuration.
- Asp, with the L configuration.

**Ring:**
- The ring closes through an ester between the Thr side-chain oxygen and the C-terminal carbonyl of the Kyn residue, written as ring closure 1 in the SMILES.
- Going around from Thr: Gly, Orn (free NH2 side chain), Asp, Ala, Asp, Gly, Ser, 3-methyl-Glu, then Kyn.
- Kyn carries a 2-aminophenyl ketone side chain.
- Ala and Ser come out D, and Orn and both ring Asp residues come out L.
- The 3-methyl-Glu carries two stereocentres, both assigned from its wedge and hash.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)c2ccccc2N)C(=O)O[C@@H]1C

name: Darobactin
text:
I read the drawing as a bicyclic peptide, written here as a SMILES string. I traced the backbone residue by residue and then assigned stereocentres from the wedges and hashes.

**Residues, N-terminus to C-terminus**
1. Trp with a free NH2. Its indole is attached through C3 to the CH2, and through C7 to the ring ether oxygen.
2. Asn, with a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
3. A residue whose alpha carbon (plain bonds, so no stereo) carries a CH(O–indole C7)(indol-3-yl) side chain. The H on the O-bearing carbon is wedged.
4. Ser (L).
5. A residue whose alpha carbon bears a CH(CH2CH2CH2NH2)(indol-6-yl) side chain. The H on that side-chain carbon is wedged.
6. Ser (L).
7. Phe (L), ending in COOH.

**Ring closures:** `%10` joins the ring ether oxygen to the CH(O) carbon. `%11` joins that carbon back to the alpha carbon of residue 3, closing the macrocycle.

**Stereochemistry:** I worked out CIP priorities and the wedge or hash direction at each drawn centre, then converted them to @/@@. The Trp, Asn, Ser and Phe alpha carbons come out S, as in L-amino acids. The CH(O) carbon is R, and the alpha carbon and side-chain carbon of residue 5 are both S. The alpha carbon of residue 3 is left unspecified because its bonds are plain.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2c1cccc2O%10)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)NC%11C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O)[C@@H](CCCN)c1ccc3c(c1)[nH]cc3[C@H]%11%10

name: Delafloxacin
text:
The structure is a quinolone (4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline-3-carboxylic acid), which I read in three parts.

**Quinolone core.** N1 bears a pyridine substituent. C2 is a CH. C3 carries the COOH and C4 is the ketone. C4a and C8a are the ring-fusion carbons. C5 is a CH. C6 carries F, C7 carries the azetidine N, and C8 carries Cl.

**Azetidine.** The ring is N–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2, a 3-hydroxyazetidin-1-yl group attached at C7.

**Pyridine substituent on N1.** The pyridine ring atoms, going around the ring, are:
- C attached to N1 of the quinolone
- C–F
- CH
- C–F
- C–NH2
- ring N, which closes back to the first carbon

From the drawing, the attachment carbon (call it C2') bonds to the ring N and to C(F) at the right. That C(F) connects to CH, then to C(F) at the top, then to C(NH2), then to the ring N. So the ring is C2'(N-quinolone), C3'(F), C4'H, C5'(F), C6'(NH2), N1'. The double bonds are C2'=C3', C4'=C5' and C6'=N1'.

**SMILES.**
- Quinolone: O=C(O)C1=CN(c2nc(N)c(F)cc2F)c2c(Cl)c(N3CC(O)C3)c(F)cc2C1=O
- Pyridine: c2nc(N)c(F)cc2F starts at C2' (bonded to N1), then ring N, then C(NH2), C(F), CH, and C(F), which closes the ring back to C2'.

Check against the drawing: C2' is bonded to N1' and to C3'(F). In the SMILES, c2 is bonded to n and, through ring closure, to the last c(F). The ring is c2 n c(N) c(F) c c2F, so the atoms are C2', N, C(NH2), C(F), CH, C(F), with C2' closing to the last C(F). That matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(O)C1=CN(c2nc(N)c(F)cc2F)c2c(Cl)c(N3CC(O)C3)c(F)cc2C1=O

name: Delamanid
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methyl-6-nitro-2,3-dihydroimidazo[2,1-b]oxazole core, in the style of delamanid-type nitroimidazooxazoles.

- **Core:** a bicyclic imidazo-oxazole carries a nitro group on the imidazole carbon next to the ring nitrogen. The quaternary carbon next to the ring oxygen bears a methyl group and a CH2–O linker.
- **Linker and aryl groups:** the CH2–O leads to a para-disubstituted benzene. This ring is attached through its other para position to the nitrogen of a piperidine. The piperidine 4-position carries an oxygen that connects to a second para-substituted benzene bearing OCF3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl on the quaternary carbon is drawn hashed, so it points away from the viewer. The remaining substituents rank ring O > CH2OAr > CH2N. Seen from the front, O (left) → CH2O (right) → CH2N (down) runs clockwise, which gives R. In the SMILES written below, this corresponds to `[C@]`.

SMILES: C[C@]1(COc2ccc(cc2)N2CCC(CC2)Oc2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc2)Cn2cc([N+](=O)[O-])nc2O1

name: Degarelix
text:
I recognised this as the decapeptide degarelix and wrote the SMILES from its known sequence, checking the stereocentres against the standard L/D conventions and the wedges in the drawing. I did not trace every wedge individually.

The sequence, read from the N-terminus, is Ac‑D‑2Nal – D‑4Cpa – D‑3Pal – L‑Ser – L‑4Aph(L‑Hor) – D‑4Aph(carbamoyl) – L‑Leu – L‑Lys(iPr) – L‑Pro – D‑Ala‑NH2. The residues are:

- **N-terminal cap and first residue:** acetyl on D‑2‑naphthylalanine.
- **Second residue:** D‑4‑chlorophenylalanine.
- **Third residue:** D‑3‑pyridylalanine.
- **Fourth residue:** L‑serine.
- **Fifth residue:** a 4‑aminophenylalanine whose side-chain amine is acylated by L‑hydroorotic acid.
- **Sixth residue:** a D‑4‑aminophenylalanine carrying a urea (carbamoyl) group.
- **Seventh residue:** L‑leucine.
- **Eighth residue:** L‑lysine with an isopropyl group on the side-chain nitrogen.
- **Ninth residue:** L‑proline.
- **C-terminus:** D‑alanine amide.
